لظ: لَظَّ 1 : see 4. === [The inf. n.] لَظٌّ is also syn. with طَرْدٌ [The act of driving away; &c.]. (Ibn- 'Abbád, K.)

لَظٌّ , (K,) or لَظٌّ كَظٌّ, (T, S, M,) A man hard, or difficult, in disposition; (S, K;) as also 🡻لَظْلَاظٌ: (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) or a man hard, o difficult, in disposition, (T, M;) and treated with severity, or rigour, (T,) or straitened; (M;) as also 🡻مِلَظٌّ and 🡻مِلْظَاظٌ: (M:) كظّ is app. an imitative sequent. (M.) You say, لَحَدِيدٌ 🡻لَظْلَاظٌإِنَّهُ Verily he is [sharp and] evil (زَعِر) in disposition. (TA.)
لظلاظ: لَظْلَاظٌ : see لَظٌّ, in two places. === It also signifies Chaste in speech; or eloquent. (TA.) === And sometimes, (Fr,) A hot day. (Fr, K.)
لظا: لَظَأٌ A little (and mean, or contemptible, TA) thing; a little. (K.)
